resolve.recipe: URL = https://trendlyne.com/equity/share-holding/<numeric_site_id>/<OUR-NSE-SYMBOL>/<period>/<company-slug>/ . <period> is 'latest' for the always-current trailing window, or a dd-mm-yyyy date, or a loose 'Qn-yyyy' alias (both accepted; observed inconsistently mixed in Trendlyne's own search-result titles). <company-slug> is cosmetic (a wrong slug still 302s/200s to the right page in our experience -- not independently verified, low risk).
resolve.id_lookup: No public search/autocomplete API was probed (avoided extra requests under the crawl-delay budget). In practice IDs were resolved via web search of 'trendlyne.com <SYMBOL> shareholding pattern' which reliably surfaces the canonical /equity/share-holding/<id>/<SYM>/... URL in the first few hits. tl_reconcile.py (already in this repo) resolves Trendlyne identities for a DIFFERENT feature (results calendar) via BSE-code/company-name matching against its free events-calendar API (trendlyne.com/equity/api/events/calendar-v2/) -- that API is unrelated to shareholding but confirms Trendlyne does expose some JSON endpoints; none was found for shareholding pattern specifically.
resolve.bulk_resolvable: UNCONFIRMED for Phase 4. No id-lookup JSON endpoint was found for shareholding. A resolver would need either (a) Trendlyne's site search/autocomplete endpoint (not probed here), or (b) a pre-built NSE-symbol -> Trendlyne-numeric-id map (does not appear to exist in this repo; tl_reconcile.py maps by BSE-code/name, not by this numeric equity id). Building one would cost ~1 request/symbol at the same rate limit as the data pull itself -- i.e. bulk sweep cost roughly doubles unless a static id map is built once and cached.

categories.Promoter > Holding: prom (sub-row; promoter total minus pledge/lock adjustments -- equals Promoter when Pledged=Locked=0, which was true for all 3 probes)
categories.Promoter > Pledged: other (promoter-pledge %, not one of our 5 fields)
categories.Promoter > Locked: other (promoter-lock %, not one of our 5 fields)
categories.FII: fii (site explicitly equates this to FPI -- narrative text on the page reads 'FII/FPI have decreased holdings from X% to Y%'; the per-quarter detail-tab row 'Foreign Portfolio Investors' carries the site's own tooltip 'identified by trendlyne as belonging to FII/FPI category', confirming the mapping directly, not inferred)
categories.DII > Banks: other (sub-row of DII; banks/FI holding, no direct field of ours)
categories.DII > Others: other (sub-row of DII; DII residual after MF/Banks/Insurance)
categories.Public: other (public non-institutional; not one of our 5 fields -- comparable to a derived-public check only, which the campaign plan (T8) says to skip)
categories.Others: unknown (a distinct top-level row alongside Promoter/FII/DII/Public, near-zero for all 3 probes; meaning not established -- possibly custodian/ADR/GDR receipts or a reconciliation residual; flag for Phase 2)
categories.Institutional (tab total) [old-format, p: fii+dii combined (NOT split on this old-format tab; site prints ONE institutional total)
categories.Institutional > Foreign Portfolio Invest: fii (tagged by the site itself as FII/FPI, see above)
categories.Institutional > Any Other [old-format]: other (includes named foreign sovereign/PE entities e.g. Abu Dhabi Investment Authority found nested here for RELIANCE Dec-2015 -- overlaps conceptually with 'DII > Others' + part of 'FII' in the current-format taxonomy; needs a Phase-2 worked example, this is the T2 trap)

subrows_shown: DII: Mutual Funds, Banks, Insurance, Others
FII: none (single row, no FPI-vs-FDI split, no country/investor-type breakdown) on the CURRENT-format summary table

old-format per-quarter detail tabs (pre-dates the current summary table's format, reachable only by visiting that specific quarter's URL): Institutional splits into Mutual Funds / Foreign Portfolio Investors / Financial Institutions-Banks / Insurance Companies / Any Other, EACH with its own 'No of holders' count and an expandable list of NAMED individual entities (e.g. 'Life Insurance Corporation of India' under Insurance Companies) -- this is much finer-grained than the current summary table but costs 1 request per quarter and is not bulk-fetchable in one page load
precision: MIXED, undocumented on-page -- top-level rows (Promoter/FII/DII/Public/Others) are displayed at 1 decimal place with inconsistent trailing-zero trimming (e.g. '50.5%' but '50%' not '50.0%' for an exact round number, and '0%' vs '0.0%' both appear across different rows in the SAME table); sub-rows (Holding/Pledged/Locked, Mutual Funds/Banks/Insurance/Others-under-DII) are displayed at 2 decimal places. The 2dp sub-rows are strictly more informative than their 1dp parent -- e.g. Promoter 'Holding' subrow can disagree with 'Promoter' parent in the 2nd decimal though they were identical for all 3 probes here since Pledged=Locked=0. Trap T6 applies: widen tolerance on the 1dp top-level rows.

Site's quarter-selector NAVIGATION (dropdown of per-quarter URLs, each showing that quarter's per-HOLDER detail only, not category totals in the same trailing-12 table) goes back further to Dec 2015 -- see access note below on how to reach it.

depth_eternal: Printed CATEGORY table: Mar 2024 (trailing 12 columns; TWO mid-quarter event rows -- Nov 29 2024 and Dec 02 2024 -- eat 2 of the 12 slots). Quarter-selector dropdown: 22-Jul-2021 (shortly after Zomato's IPO; same Trendlyne numeric id 589490 and same URL slug 'eternal-ltd' cover BOTH the ZOMATO-era and post-rename ETERNAL-era history in one continuous series -- no split, T9 is a non-issue here).

depth_probe_pre2010.verdict: NO quarter <= Jun-2010 exists ANYWHERE on Trendlyne for any of these 5 stocks. Stronger finding: the quarter-selector dropdown -- the site's full navigable inventory of shareholding-pattern periods, independent of the 12-column display cap -- bottoms out at Dec-2015 for ALL FIVE probes (RELIANCE, MCX, TCS, ITC, HDFCBANK) uniformly. This looks like a site-wide data-start date, not a per-stock listing-date artifact (all 5 were listed well before 2015). CONSEQUENCE: Trendlyne cannot help fill the pre-2010 era (0% for us, as expected) AND also cannot help fill the Sep-2010..Sep-2015 era where we are only 30.4% covered -- Trendlyne's shareholding history simply does not reach that far back for ANY stock tested.

notes_on_machine_readability: No discrete JSON API endpoint exists for shareholding-pattern data. The page is server-rendered HTML with the category table in a stable, template-generated structure (table#shareSummaryTable, one <tr> per category with rightAlgn <td> cells per column, sub-rows tagged td.p-l-3.rt-tr-group) -- trivially regex/DOM-parseable, no JS execution needed (curl-only worked for every page fetched this session). A separate chart-data convenience is also embedded as HTML data-attributes on the wrapper div (data-promoterBarChart=, data-mfBarChart=, data-fiiBarChart=) containing ready-made [[label,value,annotation],...] arrays -- but these chart arrays cover FEWER periods (9) than the table (12) and are redundant with it, not additive. One AJAX-style route was found (/equity/holding-overtime/<entity_id>/<slug>/<company-slug>/, requires header X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest or it 302-redirects) -- but it is LOGIN-WALLED ('This feature requires you to Login/Sign Up'), confirmed via a live fetch, so it is NOT usable under the hard rules and NOT a route to deeper history.
rate: 10 fetches to trendlyne.com this session (6 stock pages + 1 historical per-quarter page + 1 AJAX probe + 2 header-only checks), all HTTP 200/302 (no 403/429 seen). Self-throttled to >=10s between requests (STRICTER than the campaign's >=3s floor) because robots.txt explicitly names 'User-agent: GPTBot' and 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' with 'Crawl-delay: 10' -- honored that as the site's stated preference for AI-agent traffic even though the actual User-Agent header sent was a generic browser string (never a bot UA). Recommend Phase 3/4 planners budget 10s/request for this site, not 3s.
access_detail: The category-level summary table (our primary comparison target) requires NO login -- verified on 6 stock pages. The per-quarter individual-holder DETAIL tables (Promoter/Institutional/Public tabs, reached via a per-quarter URL) also require no login -- verified for RELIANCE 31-12-2015. ONLY the single-entity 'holding history over time' modal (the little clock/history icon next to each named holder or category row) is login-walled -- confirmed live, not attempted further per hard rules (no account created, no credentials entered).
notes: SUMMARY FOR PHASE 4 GATING: Trendlyne IS machine-readable (plain HTML, no browser needed) and IS free/open for the data that matters, BUT the useful per-stock category history is capped at a TRAILING 12-PERIOD WINDOW on every page load regardless of URL -- there is no way to page/paginate the summary table further, and no bulk multi-quarter API. To reach further back than ~2.5-3 years per stock requires ONE extra HTTP request PER quarter, landing on a differently-shaped 'old format' taxonomy (Institutional total undifferentiated into FII/DII, only splitting into named sub-categories -- see 'categories' above) that changes again somewhere in the site's own history (T2-style trap, unexplored -- when the current Promoter/FII/DII/Public/Others 5-way split supersedes the old 3-category Institutional breakdown was not determined this session). This materially affects Phase 4 sizing: a true bulk sweep of full history via this site costs roughly (1 request for the trailing window) + (1 request per additional desired quarter) per stock, i.e. up to ~40+ requests/stock for full Dec-2015-to-date depth, not 1. If Phase 4 only needs the last ~3 years per stock (which covers most of our Sep-2019-to-date 100%-covered era, our best-covered era anyway), the 1-request-per-stock route is cheap and clean. If Phase 4 wants Trendlyne to help with our weakest eras (pre-Jun-2016), it CANNOT -- Trendlyne's own data starts Dec-2015, one quarter before our worst gap (Dec-2015..Mar-2016 'seam') even opens, and covers almost none of our 30.4%-covered 2010-2015 wayback-MC era, so it is not a useful CORROBORATION source for the eras we most need external corroboration for (T3 circularity: pre-2010 unfillable by Trendlyne; 2010-2015 largely unreachable by Trendlyne too, so it can barely help break the Moneycontrol-circularity problem noted in plan T3). It IS useful corroboration for Jun-2016-onward, where the BSE-XBRL-ledger and live-NSE-XBRL eras already sit at 99.9-100% coverage.
